answer: After a hailstorm, neighbours report the largest stones they collected, and the distribution must decay with distance from the storm core exactly as radar reflectivity predicts. The stones fall in a spiral band, a quill of ice at the edge and lumps at the centre, with the zenith of the storm marking the biggest hail. A single operator cannot invent a smooth spatial gradient from one backyard, since every fake report would cluster at one size and betray the farm.
